steps.title: Treat filling as positive work
steps.content: A pipe that fills a tank contributes a positive rate. A pipe or leak that empties the tank contributes a negative rate. Add rates to find the net rate.
steps.formula:
Filling rate = 1 / time to fill
Emptying rate = −1 / time to empty
steps.example: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours, so it fills 1/6 of the tank per hour.

steps.title: Combine two filling pipes
steps.prompt: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and B in 3 hours. How long do they take together?
steps.explanation: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 tank per hour. Time = 2 hours.

steps.title: Include a leak
steps.content: Subtract the leak's emptying rate from the filling rate. If a pipe fills in a hours and a leak empties in b hours, net rate is 1/a − 1/b when the leak is active.
steps.example: A pipe fills in 4 hours; a leak empties in 12 hours. Net rate = 1/4−1/12 = 1/6, so the tank fills in 6 hours.

steps.title: Find the net time
steps.prompt: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours. A leak empties it in 24 hours. How long to fill with the leak open?
steps.explanation: Net rate = 1/8−1/24 = 2/24 = 1/12 tank per hour. Time = 12 hours.

steps.title: Work with changing pipes
steps.content: When a pipe is opened or closed partway through, calculate work completed in each time interval separately, then add the remaining fraction.
steps.tip: Use fractions of one tank as the unit of work; avoid adding the times directly.
